main_issue: Whether alcohol can be served at the housewarming in the flat, resolved by keeping the drinks in a cooler box outside the front door

A-B.evidence: Turn 2 B: 'looks good to me' (A's drinks fine). Turns 17 and 19: both accept the cooler outside; they never address each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C asks A at turn 15 about the cooler outside; A answers at turn 17 'a cooler outside works for me'. C had no stated position before proposing.

A-D.evidence: At turn 4 D objects to alcohol; at turn 8 A questions it. D accepts outside the door at turn 14, A accepts at 17, and A says 'that's settled' at 21.

B-C.evidence: C asks B at turn 18 if the cooler is okay for the manager; B at turn 19: 'that works for me... Thanks for sorting it out.'

B-D.evidence: B needs drinks available for the manager (turn 10) while D wants no alcohol (turn 9). Both accept the cooler outside (turns 14, 19).

C-D.evidence: C offers the kitchen (11), which D rejects (12). C then proposes the cooler outside (13) and D agrees: 'I can agree to that. Thanks, Agent C' (14).
